name: Mallow Red
lede: Mallow Red is a muted, purplish crimson named for the mallow flower, close kin to mauve.

sections.title: A flower's red
sections.body:
Paterson defines mallows (mallow) red as a deep crimson or purplish red, and mallow alone as reddish-purple [1][2]. The flower is the same one behind mauve: Paterson notes that mauve took its name in France from the purple streaks in the mallow flower [3]. So mallow red and [[mauve]] are two ends of one source, a flower seen as red and a flower seen as purple.

Maerz and Paul record mallow red as first used in 1862, on plate 51 [4]. That date falls just after Perkin's aniline purple turned flower-purples into fashion [3][4]. The books do not say whether the two events are connected.

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: Mallow Red is rare in painting [5]. Only 3 of 23,781 paintings in our archive cover at least 5% of their canvas with it, as photographed [5]. Two are early modern: Matisse's *Woman on a Terrace* (1907), where it covers about 18%, and Kirchner's *Two Girls under an Umbrella* (1910), about 15% [5]. Its nearest standard name is [[mauve]], 6.7 ΔE away, and the nearest listed pink is France Rose [4]. Related names: [[mauvette]], [[crimson]] and [[magenta]].
